title: AI-Use Attestation to Keep SMB Liability Cover
one_liner: As liability policies exclude generative AI, small firms need underwriter-ready proof of AI controls to win affirmative cover, and independent agencies need a renewal ritual that keeps them relevant.
customer: Independent insurance agencies (about 37k remain) that place GL and E&O for law firms, accountants, marketing agencies, clinics and contractors, plus those SMB clients.
problem: ISO's gen-AI exclusion is already on thousands of CGL policies (Insurance Business, 2026-09-16). AI-specialist insurers target tech firms, not a dental practice using an AI receptionist. Agencies can't advise and carriers haven't said what evidence they'd accept, so clients discover the gap at claim time.
solution: A lightweight AI Use Register: discover which AI tools staff use (SSO and browser discovery), apply policy templates and human-review logging, and output a standardized attestation that a panel of MGAs and carriers agree to accept for endorsements or premium credits. Agencies white-label it into their renewal workflow.
why_now: Exclusions are spreading now, independent agencies are shrinking (39k in 2024 to 37k in 2026, Insurance Journal) yet still sell 95% of commercial insurance through humans, and insurtech's dollars (99.1% of Q2 funding is AI-centric) go to back-office tools, not SMB risk evidence.
revenue_model: $49-$149 per month per SMB, billed via the agency or the client, plus MGA per-policy referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Carriers don't yet know what evidence they want, so whoever standardizes the artifact defines it, as cyber questionnaires and scans did for Coalition and At-Bay. Agencies get a reason to call every client at renewal.
first_30_days: Interview five underwriters on what evidence they'd accept. Ship a spreadsheet-and-form v0 of the register. Sell it to 10 agencies through state agent-association chapters and get 30 SMBs onto paid plans.

title: Fake-Support Scam Takedown for Fintechs
one_liner: A monitoring and takedown service that finds scammers posing as your customer support in public help threads, clusters them by phone, WhatsApp and Telegram identifiers, and kills them fast with regulator-ready evidence files.
customer: Fraud, trust & safety and CX heads at crypto exchanges, wallet makers, neobanks, BNPL and payment providers. Start with mid-market crypto/fintech ($5M-$50M ARR), then EU payment service providers. Roughly $3k-$10k per month.
problem: Every 'my account is locked' thread in a fintech or crypto subreddit gets a friendly stranger reply within minutes, then a DM pushing a WhatsApp or Telegram 'support agent'. Mods remove the comments, but the brand never sees removed comments or DMs. The same 20-50 phone numbers and handles recycle week after week, and victims are usually novices or seniors. Mods keep private spreadsheets of these identifiers, and nobody aggregates them for the brand being impersonated.
solution: Monitor public help venues (Reddit through licensed access or partners, plus X, Facebook groups, YouTube comments, Google Business listings, review-site replies and search ads) for support-impersonation patterns. Extract the contact identifiers, graph-cluster them into campaigns, and file takedowns with WhatsApp/Telegram, telcos, registrars and platforms. Produce timestamped evidence packs for refund disputes and regulators. Give each brand a pre-registered 'official support channels' beacon that community mods can add to a sticky or AutoMod reply for free, cutting victim conversion without any content moderation. Mods are never paid, and the data flows to them.
why_now: The EU PSR/PSD3 political agreement of 27 November 2025 makes payment providers refund customers in bank-employee impersonation scams and makes online platforms liable to those providers if they fail to remove notified fraudulent content. Notification evidence and takedown speed now have a dollar value. The UK's mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement (since October 2024) already priced this risk. LLM-written scam scripts are fluent, which defeats keyword filters.
revenue_model: SaaS subscription of $3k-$10k per month per brand, a per-takedown premium tier, evidence-pack retainers for payment providers in the EU, and later an identifier feed sold to telcos and platforms.
non_obvious_insight: The scam's weak point is the contact channel, not the message. Fluent AI text is cheap, but the phone numbers, handles and domains are a small recyclable set, so identifier graphs beat content classifiers. Mod removal logs also hold the ground truth on how many minutes a scam reply survives, which brands can't see and which now matters for liability. An 'official channels' sticky is the cheapest conversion-killer there is.
first_30_days: Build a free 'exposure audit' for 10 mid-size crypto and fintech brands: a 30-day scan of public threads, X and Google Business listings that shows them 40 live scam identifiers and how long each survived. Send each fraud lead their own brand's data. Convert 2 into $2.5k/month paid pilots. Partner with 3 volunteer mod teams of fintech subreddits, giving them free tooling and taking labeled ground truth in return, with no payment to mods.

title: File-Cabinet-to-Pipeline Digitization Crew
one_liner: A mobile scan-and-extract crew that turns a newly acquired trades company's filing cabinets and paper job files into a clean customer and equipment-age database plus a ready-to-run replacement and membership campaign.
customer: Acquirers of legacy HVAC, plumbing, roofing, pest, electrical and garage-door companies (search funders, holdcos, PE add-on platforms). The buyer pays a fixed fee plus a share of revenue from jobs sold off the output. Brokers are a secondary channel, using it as sell-side data-room prep.
problem: Acquired trades firms often run on paper, desk phones and old PCs, so the owner cannot see permit errors, warranty problems or job margins. Any AI, field-service software or roll-up integration needs structured data first. Meanwhile decades of installs sit in file drawers as an unused equipment-age database.
solution: A two-person crew with document scanners and phone capture spends 5-10 days on site. Vision-model extraction pulls customer, address, equipment make/model/serial, install date, service history, warranty status and membership status. Output is import-ready for ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro and QuickBooks, plus an 'asset-age' list: homes with systems older than a set threshold, expiring warranties, lapsed maintenance customers and contract renewals. It includes a letter/SMS campaign and prepaid-membership offer templates, with job tagging so results are measured.
why_now: Handwriting and form extraction from photos became accurate and cheap in 2025-2026. Bain's 2026 GP outlook says 39% of GPs expect no material financial impact from AI on portfolio companies this year, and Bain's midyear report says leaders redesign workflows rather than layering tools on top. Both point to data readiness as the gap. First-time buyers of small trades firms are more numerous than ever, and each faces the same digitization backlog.
revenue_model: $8-15K fixed fee per business, plus 8-10% of first-year revenue from jobs tagged to campaigns generated from the output. Sell-side version for brokers: $3-5K data-room prep before listing.
non_obvious_insight: What looks like clutter is a proprietary, geocoded equipment-age database of thousands of households, the highest-intent lead list in the trades, and the buyer paid for it in the purchase price without knowing. Rob Brooks found '30,000 customer records' in filing cabinets, 13-year-old computers and desk phones, could not see permit or warranty problems until he digitized, and reached $1.3M EBITDA from $340K SDE in 14 months with about 800 customers prepaying three years of membership (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/rob-brooks-gary-air). Winsor Fireform's buyers spent seven months digitizing roughly 90% paper records (https://acquiringminds.co/articles/andrew-sova-alex-clark-winsor-fireform-novo-foundry). Tew & Taylor ran on Excel and mailed checks, creating a large receivables backlog (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/jack-rauch-tew-taylor). Bain's GP outlook notes 39% of GPs see no material AI impact on portfolios in 2026 (https://www.bain.com/insights/private-equitys-reality-check-gp-outlook-2026/). Every buyer solved digitization ad hoc, and none treated the archive as revenue.
first_30_days: Pick HVAC in one metro. Find 3 recent small-business buyers through ETA communities and brokers, and offer one a near-cost pilot. Scan and extract 2,000 records in 3 days, mail letters or SMS to the oldest-equipment homes, and count booked calls per 500 contacts. Publish the result as a case study, then price the service at $8-15K plus revenue share. Meanwhile approach 5 HVAC business brokers with the sell-side data-room version.

title: Hour-Meter Forensics for Used Farm Equipment
one_liner: An independent inspection and identity report for used tractors and combines that cross-checks engine-hour logs across ECUs, serial numbers and liens to catch rolled-back hours and phantom sellers.
customer: Used-equipment dealers and auction houses, equipment-finance lenders and Farm Credit associations, and farmers buying $100K-800K machines on classifieds and marketplaces.
problem: Used machine value is driven by hours. Tools that roll back hour meters and ECU logs are openly sold, and buyers wire deposits to fake sellers. Lien and ownership checks are patchy. Row crops are projected to lose money for a fourth straight year and farm bankruptcies are up 19%, so lenders care about collateral and farmers buy used. Historically independent shops could not read OEM diagnostics, so no neutral party could verify a machine's history.
solution: Mobile mechanics with OEM-capable diagnostic tools pull hour counts from every module (engine, transmission, monitor, telematics) and compare them, review calibration and replacement logs, and flag mismatches. An identity module checks the serial against photos, runs a UCC lien search and does seller KYC, with escrow released on inspection. Output is a signed 'Hours Verified' certificate, later an API for lenders and auction platforms.
why_now: Deere's $99M settlement obliges it to open its diagnostic and repair tools for 10 years, creating independent access to the machine's real history for the first time. Repair restrictions cost farmers about $4.2B a year. Squeezed farm incomes push demand toward used machines, and leaked ID data feeds synthetic seller identities.
revenue_model: $195-495 per inspection paid by buyer or lender, $99 per lot from auction houses, a 0.5-1% escrow fee, and per-collateral fees from lenders for portfolio audits.
non_obvious_insight: Right-to-repair created a security market. Once independent shops can read what a machine really did, its history becomes a verifiable identity, a Carfax-like asset that OEM dealers, who profit from service and trade-ins, are structurally reluctant to publish. Whoever publishes trusted hours first owns the data asset.
first_30_days: Hire two ag mechanics who already own diagnostic tools. Offer a $150 'Hours Check' at three auction houses and five independent dealers during fall auction season. Publish the discrepancy rate as a case study. Then pitch equipment-finance lenders and Farm Credit associations a free 30-machine collateral audit.

title: Licensed Cozy Games for Memory Care
one_liner: A turnkey activity program for senior living made of commercially licensed cozy indie games, in a kiosk kit that logs resident participation for compliance paperwork.
customer: Activity directors and operators of memory care, assisted living and skilled nursing communities, starting with independents and small regional chains of 5-50 sites. They pay about $199-349 a month per community plus a $349-499 kit.
problem: Nursing homes must run person-centered activity programs and document participation (CMS F-tag 679). Directors are short on budget and staff time. Existing tech is expensive proprietary hardware such as projector tables or VR. Consumer games are the wrong fit: their licences forbid commercial and public use, and they have reading-heavy UI, timers and fail states.
solution: A curated library of 30-50 indie titles that are gentle by design: no fail states, no timers, big targets, little text, familiar themes like gardening, cooking and tidying. Developers grant commercial, DRM-free licences for a revenue share. Each title runs in a locked kiosk launcher on a docked handheld or mini-PC to the TV, with big-button controllers. Staff get 5-minute group-play cards and a one-tap participation log that exports to activity documentation. It is positioned as activity programming, not therapy, so it makes no clinical claims.
why_now: About 4M Americans turn 65 each year through 2027, so demand for senior activities is rising. Handheld PCs are cheap and reliable. Senior living operators are already piloting games (for example the Belmont Village pilot of a cognitive game). Steam's glut of cozy games means many strong titles with dormant back-catalogs that earn nothing.
revenue_model: Monthly subscription per community, a hardware kit margin, and 40-50% of subscription revenue paid to developers by playtime. Later: enterprise contracts with chains, and reimbursement or wellness-budget channels.
non_obvious_insight: Steam keys are personal-use licences. Only the developer can grant commercial or public-performance rights, and a dormant catalog makes them say yes for a small guarantee. The traits that make cozy games sell are exactly what dementia-friendly design needs. And directors buy relief from documentation and set-up time, not cognitive outcomes. VCs file this under 'brain-training edtech', while an insider sees a licensing arbitrage plus a compliance workflow.
first_30_days: License 8-10 cozy titles, offering $500 minimum guarantees plus revenue share. Assemble 5 kits at about $400 each. Offer free 4-week pilots to 5 local communities through activity-director Facebook groups and state activity-professional associations. Log participation minutes per resident. Convert pilots to paid at week 5.

title: Pre-Confirmation Screwworm Risk Feed for Cattle Markets
one_liner: A county-level early-warning feed that fuses news, vet reports, weather and zone announcements to give cattle buyers, auction barns and insurers days or weeks of lead time over official lab confirmation.
customer: Auction markets and sale barns, feedlots and stocker buyers, livestock lenders and insurers, and cattle-futures or ag-commodity desks. Ranchers and vet clinics are a low-price tier.
problem: New World screwworm has reached Texas and New Mexico. The UC San Diego team building a tracker says official reporting lags: 'Lab confirmation can take days or weeks.' Cattle prices, hauling rules and purchase decisions move on rumor and news before confirmation. Producers have no single source for zone status and their own exposure.
solution: A subscription feed that scores county-level risk from public and semi-public signals: state and APHIS zone announcements, extension and vet-clinic posts, local news, trap and case reports, and fly-friendly temperature and humidity. It sends SMS or email alerts and a plain-language 'movement readiness' checklist for each zone. Users can submit their own sightings, which improves the model. Sold in tiers from a $99/month producer plan to trading-desk contracts.
why_now: The screwworm reached the US Southwest in 2026, and APHIS newsroom items on 18 and 21 September 2026 show Texas releasing infested zones. The academic dashboard is a research tool, not a commercial product, and the sterile-fly response is slow to scale, so risk and compliance uncertainty will last through at least one fly season.
revenue_model: Producer and barn subscriptions at $99-500/month, insurer, lender and buyer contracts at $2-10k/month, and enterprise API fees for commodity desks.
non_obvious_insight: The academic value of the dashboard is the reporting lag itself: the UC San Diego team added media reports because 'lab confirmation can take days or weeks' (https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/09/260914102439.htm). The paying customer is anyone whose money moves on news before USDA confirms, meaning buyers, hedgers and insurers, not the county health officials the tool was built for. The lag is the product. Recent APHIS announcements show zone status is changing week to week (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/news).
first_30_days: Build a scraper and manual-curation pipeline over APHIS and Texas Animal Health Commission announcements, extension and vet feeds, and local news, plus a weather-based fly-activity index. Publish a free weekly map to gather emails. Pitch 10 sale barns and 3 commodity or insurer desks a paid pilot and sell the first 5 at a founding discount. Contact the UC San Diego team about a data and methods collaboration. Note that the APHIS screwworm page consulted in this session still said the pest was absent from the US, so confirm current case status before launch.

title: Code-Cleared Church Space for Microschools
one_liner: Pair congregations with empty classroom wings and microschool or childcare operators, and sell the missing piece: pre-cleared zoning, fire and licensing paths.
customer: Microschool founders, learning-pod operators and small childcare providers who pay rent, and shrinking congregations, lodges and libraries with weekday space. Operators pay a platform fee; congregations pay for readiness passports.
problem: Microschool enrollment has grown an estimated 40% since 2023, and ESAs plus a federal scholarship tax credit starting in 2027 will add demand. Space is not the constraint; permission is. Certificate-of-occupancy, fire-marshal, egress, sprinkler and childcare-licensing rules vary by jurisdiction, so operators guess and congregations do not know what their building could legally host.
solution: For each listed building, produce a jurisdiction-specific readiness passport: occupancy class, likely deficiencies with cost estimates, pre-drawn plan sets, checklist and sequencing for approvals. Add a standard lease, child-protection policy pack and insurance bundle. Operators search by county and see how many weeks and dollars separate them from opening.
why_now: ESAs, tax-credit scholarships and state laws (Florida now lets registered microschools use former churches and similar buildings without zoning changes) are moving faster than building codes. Congregations are shrinking and buildings are costly to maintain. Treasury rulemaking on what counts as a school adds uncertainty that rewards jurisdiction-specific expertise.
revenue_model: $2k to $6k per building readiness passport, 5% of first-year rent or $250 to $500 a month platform fee from operators, insurance referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Listing space is a commodity. Pre-cleared certainty is the product, and the code-path knowledge compounds jurisdiction by jurisdiction. Each solved county becomes a reusable playbook and a barrier to competitors.
first_30_days: Pick one state that has ESAs and friendly rules (Florida, Texas, Arizona or Tennessee). Map the approval path in 3 counties. Sign 5 churches and 5 microschool operators through founder groups. Deliver the first paid passport for $3k with a code consultant.

title: Peer-Made Aide Training in Creole, Spanish, Tagalog
one_liner: A library of short scenario videos made by experienced home-care aides in their own languages, RN-reviewed and sold to agencies as required in-service training that keeps new aides from quitting.
customer: Home-care agencies, home health agencies and nursing homes in immigrant-heavy states (NY, FL, MA, NJ, CA). The buyer is the training or HR lead, paying per aide.
problem: Agency turnover runs 77-80% and roughly 4 in 5 new caregivers quit within 100 days. 30% of direct care workers are immigrants (60% in New York), and about 350,000 Haitians lost TPS on Aug 4. Federal rules require annual in-service hours for home health aides and nursing-home nurse aides (12 hours a year, and states add more), and most content is English-language corporate e-learning or AI-dubbed avatars that workers ignore and that can be clinically wrong.
solution: Recruit working aides who already post in Haitian Creole, Spanish, Tagalog or Arabic on Facebook, TikTok and WhatsApp. They shoot 3 to 6 minute scenarios (transfers, dementia redirection, refusing a bath, safe lifting). An RN reviews each script, and the clip carries a 'peer-made, RN-verified' provenance stamp. The platform adds quizzes, attendance logs for surveyors, and a first-week mentor-video track aimed at the 100-day cliff. Creators get 35-40% of revenue plus a bonus for completion.
why_now: Visa pauses and TPS terminations are reshuffling the workforce by language group right now. The federal nursing-home staffing mandate was repealed (Feb 2026), which leaves retention as the agencies' only lever. AI slop training content is flooding the market, and creators are hunting for income beyond ad revenue.
revenue_model: $9-14 per aide per month billed to the agency (a 75-aide agency pays about $700-1,000), sold as an annual contract. About 35-40% goes to creators. A later add-on covers state-approved CE credits and dementia-training modules.
non_obvious_insight: Aides do not quit because training is bad. They quit because nobody who looks or sounds like them says the job gets easier. A peer in your language who has survived the first 100 days is a retention device that also happens to satisfy a compliance line item, and an AI avatar cannot supply that credibility.
first_30_days: Find 5 aide-creators through Creole, Spanish and Tagalog Facebook groups and workforce training programs. Partner with a per-diem RN reviewer. Shoot 20 scenarios in 3 weeks and pitch 5 agencies (start with Miami, Boston and NYC) on a 90-day pilot at a free-first-month price tied to a measured 100-day retention improvement.

title: Fire-Loss Data Co-op and Parametric MRF Cover
one_liner: Pool waste-facility fire data to price the unpriced battery-fire risk, then offer verified premium credits and fast-paying parametric cover.
customer: MRFs, transfer stations, scrap yards and e-scrap recyclers (pay verification and premium), with specialty brokers, MGAs and reinsurers buying the data.
problem: August 2026 saw 49 facility fires (tied for the 10-year August high), 293 year to date, and 74 catastrophic (over $400K) versus 71 in all of 2024. Public counts cover only two-alarm-plus events, and actual totals may be about 6x higher. Severe incidents average about $1.5M and no one has decided who pays.
solution: Step 1 is a fire-risk score and controls-verification certificate (thermal cameras, suppression, inbound inspection, tip-floor separation). Step 2 is an anonymized incident and thermal-alert data co-op. Step 3 is an MGA arrangement with a fronting carrier offering premium credits for verified controls and a parametric top-up that pays a fixed amount when a verified thermal event crosses a threshold, for fast cleanup and business-interruption cash.
why_now: Losses are concentrating and rising, states are still arguing about liability, and BRACE Act storage-permit debates put battery handling in the spotlight. The expected next step is insurers repricing, adding exclusions or demanding sensors, so verified data becomes the currency.
revenue_model: $2-5K per site per year for verification, a 10-15% MGA commission on placed premium, and data licensing to insurers and reinsurers.
non_obvious_insight: The unpriced risk here is data, not fire physics. The industry's own public numbers understate reality by roughly 6x, so the first party with a real loss dataset sets the price.
first_30_days: Compile a scrubbed fire dataset from trackers, news, fire-department reports and OSHA logs and derive loss-cost bands. Interview 5 specialty brokers. Recruit 5 facilities for a pilot with an off-the-shelf thermal camera package. Open talks with a fronting carrier.

title: Succession Roll-Up for Retiring Solo Therapists
one_liner: A service that brokers and buys retiring solo practices and transitions clients to vetted associates, so clients are not orphaned and young clinicians inherit a full caseload.
customer: Retiring psychologists, social workers and family therapists (paid through fees and earn-outs) and early-career clinicians or group practices paying a transition fee, roughly $3-10k per practice.
problem: A large share of independent therapists are past 55, and solo practitioners typically just close, leaving clients scrambling. New clinicians spend 12-24 months building a caseload. Consolidation is capturing platform-dependent supply (Spring Health acquiring Alma, Jan 2026; Universal Health Services buying Talkspace for $835M, Mar 2026), but nobody owns practice transition the way dental service organizations do.
solution: A 6-12 month warm-handoff program consistent with ethics codes and client choice: records custody, client consent workflow, payer-panel reassignment through a group NPI, referral-source handover, and an earn-out to the retiring clinician funded by the successor's collections. Software handles consent, records and payer onboarding. Later: an MSO owning the transitioned practices.
why_now: Back-office rails built by Alma and Grow (Grow raised $150M) now make onboarding an associate cheap. Boomer therapists retire through 2025-30, and platform consolidation leaves the independent tail unowned.
revenue_model: Transition fee (5-10% of annual practice revenue), earn-out spread, later MSO margin, and buyer-side subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is consolidating the platform, but nobody is consolidating the goodwill of retiring clinicians, which is the cheapest source of established caseloads and referral relationships and the one asset that walks out the door every Friday.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 retiring clinicians through state association mailings and Psychology Today profiles. Match five with early-career clinicians. Have a healthcare attorney draft an ethics-reviewed transition agreement, and complete two transitions at a flat $3k each.

title: AI Standardized Clients for Counseling Programs
one_liner: Voice-based AI 'clients' with persistent backstories, scored on accredited-skills rubrics, give master's students hundreds of rehearsal sessions before real practicum.
customer: Counseling, social-work and MFT master's programs (CACREP-accredited and similar), then OT and PT programs for patient-interview training; the department or a student lab fee pays.
problem: Practicum placements and faculty supervision are scarce. Human standardized clients cost about $30-60 an hour, and classmate role-plays are low fidelity. The new loan caps squeeze programs in excluded fields, and students need repetitions in high-stakes skills like suicide-risk assessment and motivational interviewing.
solution: Real-time voice client agents that stay consistent across sessions, remember last week, vary in difficulty and present safety-critical scenarios. Sessions are auto-scored on rubrics (reflective listening, risk questions asked, missed cues), supervisors review flagged clips, and sessions are logged as pre-practicum skills hours. Rehearsal volume is multiplied, not supervised hours replaced.
why_now: Low-latency, natural voice models with long-term memory reached usable fidelity in 2025-26. Programs in excluded fields face cost pressure after July 2026, and therapist demand remains strong.
revenue_model: $75-200 per student per semester as a lab fee, or $15-40k site licenses per program.
non_obvious_insight: What was infeasible was a client who stays consistent over sessions and reacts with emotion in real time. The binding constraint in clinical training is rehearsal volume, which is exactly what AI supplies cheaply, without threatening the human-supervised hours that licensure requires.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 counseling programs through adjunct faculty who teach skills labs. Build 6 scenarios (intake, motivational interviewing, suicide risk) and run a spring pilot. Measure improvement on the program's existing skills rubric and price at about $100 per student. Build in clinical safety review and privacy controls.

title: Disaster-Day Instant Cash Parametric Cover
one_liner: Pay a fixed sum to a household's phone within hours of an official evacuation order or multi-day power shutoff, funded by cheap capital that is hunting for granular parametric risk.
customer: Employers, HOAs, utilities, school districts and credit unions in wildfire, flood and hurricane zones that buy group cover for employees or members. Also mortgage servicers for at-risk borrowers.
problem: After an evacuation order, households spend hundreds of dollars a day on hotels, fuel, food and pet boarding before any additional-living-expense claim is paid. Renters and FAIR plan or nonrenewed homeowners often lack that cover entirely. Claims take weeks.
solution: A parametric micro-policy paying $500-$2,000 within hours when an official evacuation order, extended power shutoff, or verified flood depth covers the insured address. Triggers come from public alert feeds and utility notices, and payment goes to a debit card or wallet. An MGA fronts it with ILS-backed capacity.
why_now: Reinsurance is softening and cat bond capital is at a record ($65.6B outstanding), so granular parametric capacity is cheap. Instant rails are mature, and nonrenewals and FAIR plan reliance are growing.
revenue_model: $5-$15 per household per month, an MGA margin of 20-30%, and group distribution fees.
non_obvious_insight: Instant cash, not indemnity, is the product, and small payouts make basis risk tolerable. Institutions with a duty of care buy per head, so a single sale reaches hundreds of households.
first_30_days: Pilot with a rural credit union and one WUI-county employer or school district. Find a parametric MGA to front it, run a synthetic-trigger payout test, and sign a paid 90-day pilot.

title: Unfreeze Desk for Indian UPI Merchants
one_liner: A court-ready dossier generator and fixed-fee advocate network that unfreezes shopkeepers' bank accounts after a scam victim's UPI money passes through them, with a freeze-continuity layer later.
customer: Small merchants, traders, fuel-station owners and freelancers in India whose current or savings accounts get frozen because a scam victim's money passed through their UPI QR. They pay per case (₹3,000-8,000) or a ₹199/month subscription. Chartered accountants and trader associations are the referral channel.
problem: Automated cyber-fraud freezes catch innocent recipients. One Faridabad scam of ₹4.43 crore led to more than 36,000 frozen accounts, mostly small merchants. A Mumbai shop owner was frozen over ₹826 and spent over a month trying to get access back. A retailer's ₹8.26 lakh current account was blocked over a single ₹1,000 UPI payment. Relief takes months, and working capital, payroll and supplier payments stall.
solution: Merchants upload the bank statement and freeze notice, and software extracts the flagged credit, payer VPA, invoices and merchant-vintage evidence. It then produces a bundle for the bank nodal officer and police investigating officer, and a draft writ petition citing the Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Rajasthan High Court rulings that a merchant cannot verify each UPI payer. Partner advocates file and appear at a fixed fee, and the tool tracks the case. Phase 2: a 'clean receipts' setup (order-ID dynamic QR, invoice per payment, a separate working-capital account) and an NBFC-funded bridge advance against the frozen balance.
why_now: The Andhra Pradesh High Court ruled in July 2026 that authorities cannot freeze a merchant's whole account for receiving a UPI payment from an accused, and other High Courts have said the same. That gives a template-able legal remedy where before it was ad hoc. The Faridabad freezes and the Home Ministry review put the problem in the news. UPI acceptance among tiny merchants keeps growing.
revenue_model: Fixed case fee of ₹3,000-8,000 (unfreeze package plus advocate), a ₹199/month 'Merchant Shield' subscription that keeps an evidence dossier updated, and referral fees from NBFC partners for frozen-balance bridge loans. Later B2B licensing to UPI QR aggregators and bank merchant-onboarding teams.
non_obvious_insight: The merchant is not defrauded. The loss is working capital held hostage by a blunt automated tool that recovers almost nothing, so banks over-freeze. A Parliamentary Standing Committee found only ₹0.57 crore recovered out of ₹2,294.79 crore lost to cyber fraud in 2022, about 0.02%. So the freeze is structural false-positive management, not an anti-fraud problem, and the buyer is desperate on day one. Police in Faridabad said 'People come crying. Some had only ₹200 or ₹500 transferred to their accounts, yet the banks froze them.' Evidence: https://the420.in/faridabad-cyber-scam-upi-fraud-accounts-frozen-home-ministry/ and https://www.medianama.com/2026/07/223-merchants-bank-accounts-frozen-upi-payments-fraudsters-andhra-hc/.
first_30_days: Days 1-5: Build a WhatsApp intake bot and landing page in Hindi and English ('Account freeze ho gaya? 10 minute mein case file'). Sign 3 partner advocates in Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Hyderabad at a fixed split. Days 5-15: Template the dossier and petition from the three High Court rulings and have the advocates review it. Post explainer videos in Hindi and Gujarati on YouTube and Reels, and in trader WhatsApp and Telegram groups where frozen merchants already vent. Days 15-30: Close the first 20-30 paid cases, publish anonymized turnaround times, and approach two CA firms and one trader association for referrals. The design must keep filings with licensed advocates to avoid unauthorized-practice issues.

title: Scam Recovery Desk for Community Banks
one_liner: Banks buy scam detection, but the untapped money is recovery: stablecoin issuers, receiving banks and exchanges can freeze funds if someone asks fast and correctly.
customer: Community banks and credit unions ($500M-$10B assets) that increasingly eat scam reimbursements. American Banker (2026-07-22) puts bank-side scam losses at $68B, against the FTC's $15.9B of consumer-reported losses.
problem: A community bank's fraud analyst has hours before funds move on. They don't know who to call at receiving banks, exchanges or issuer compliance desks. They have no standard evidence pack, so recoveries run to a few percent and losses are written off as a cost of doing business.
solution: A 24/7 recovery desk plus software. When a victim reports a scam, the desk traces the funds (wire, Zelle and ACH recall, plus on-chain tracing for crypto off-ramps). It sends recall, 314(b) and law-enforcement freeze requests with pre-validated evidence packs to a maintained directory of receiving-institution and issuer contacts, then tracks outcomes. The desk is paid a share of every dollar recovered.
why_now: FTC losses hit a record $15.9B in 2025, and scam flows increasingly touch stablecoins. The Senate Democrats' Tether report (2026-09-28) raises pressure on issuers to respond quickly, and GENIUS-era issuers must be able to honor lawful freeze orders (verify exact text).
revenue_model: 15-25% contingency on recovered funds plus a flat monthly retainer for 24/7 coverage.
non_obvious_insight: Recovery rates depend on speed and relationships, not analytics, so a maintained contact directory and playbook is an operations moat. Stablecoins are counterintuitively the most freezable scam rail, more so than wires or Zelle, if you know the freeze path.
first_30_days: Offer five community banks a free post-mortem of their last 90 days of scam cases and estimate the recoverable share. Hire two ex-bank fraud investigators. Sign two contingency pilots and build the first version of the issuer and receiving-bank contact directory.

title: Data Centers Fund Neighborhood Batteries in Emerging Cities
one_liner: Sell data-center developers in capacity-starved emerging cities a bring-your-own-capacity package delivered as batteries and solar at nearby small businesses, dispatched to the local utility at the evening peak.
customer: Colocation and edge data-center developers (5-100 MW) in cities such as Nairobi, Lagos, Johannesburg, Cape Town, Johor and Sao Paulo.
problem: Data-center projects are stalling on power and social license: Equinix's Cape Town plan (174 MW, 4.4B liters of water a year) drew protests and Kenya's 1 GW G42-Microsoft project is stalled. Utilities cannot add capacity quickly, gas turbines are sold out through 2029-30 at about $2,157/kW, and PJM now makes large loads bring their own capacity or curtail. In emerging cities, nearby small businesses already suffer outages and run diesel gensets.
solution: An aggregator finances 1-5 MWh of C&I batteries and solar at hundreds of businesses near the data center's substation (cold rooms, clinics, schools, bakeries, malls), with leases funded by the data center's capacity fee. The businesses get outage protection, and 20-30% of each battery is reserved for evening-peak dispatch, metered and verified. The developer gets a firm capacity certificate for its utility filing and a community-benefit story: the neighborhood's evening peak falls and outages drop by a stated number of hours.
why_now: Bring-your-own-capacity is now the template (PJM's backstop auction and curtailment proposals, Voltus selling 100 MW to Google, Sunrun, Tesla and Renew Home pitching 16.8 GW of capacity-as-a-service). The Duke study shows flexibility could unlock 76 GW at 0.25% curtailment, stationary batteries are around $70/kWh, and the 100-500 kWh C&I band is underserved because suppliers set roughly 10 MW minimums.
revenue_model: A capacity fee from the data center, benchmarked to PJM's $325-555 per MW-day (roughly $120-200 per kW-year) and to be validated locally, on 10-15 year terms, plus lease income from the small businesses and dispatch or demand-response revenue from the utility.
non_obvious_insight: The data center's real willingness to pay is set by the cost of delay (about $14M a month for an idle 60 MW site) and by permit risk, not by the value of the kWh. In emerging cities the marginal capacity is neighbors' diesel gensets, so replacing them with batteries is both the cheapest firm capacity and the way to defuse local opposition.
first_30_days: Pick one stuck project (a 20-50 MW edge or colo site in Nairobi, Lagos or Johannesburg), reach the developer's power or permitting lead, and propose a paid 500 kWh pilot. Sign 15-20 businesses within 3 km of the substation, log feeder evening-peak load before and after, and deliver a feeder-impact report as the pitch asset.

title: Mini Cat Bonds for Co-ops and Counties
one_liner: Cat bond capital is at record highs but deals under $50M are uneconomic. Make a $5-25M cat bond a 90-day, low-cost, template product for the sponsors the market ignores.
customer: Small public risk pools, rural electric cooperatives, counties, hospital systems and small regional insurers needing $5M-$50M of catastrophe protection.
problem: Cat bond issuance is a record $18.9B year to date with $65.6B outstanding, yet legal, modeling, rating and SPV costs of $1M-plus put small deals out of reach. Small sponsors stay in the traditional market or go bare, while primary property markets stay hard.
solution: A standardized private cat bond or collateralized reinsurance template: pre-approved documents, standard parametric triggers with an independent calculation agent, treasury-fund collateral with transparent accounting, and a target all-in cost under $150k with issuance in about 90 days. Sell the notes to ILS funds seeking diversification.
why_now: Record traditional and ILS capital, softening through 2027 (Jefferies), and mature tokenized and money-market collateral (Goldman put a $100B Treasury fund into crypto plumbing, CoinDesk 2026-09-28). ILS investors want diversification beyond Florida wind.
revenue_model: 1.5-3% of limit as a structuring fee, plus annual administration and calculation-agent fees.
non_obvious_insight: Softening means capital wants to deploy, so the binding constraint is deal cost per dollar of limit. That is a documentation and operations problem, not a risk-appetite problem.
first_30_days: Retain an offshore law firm and a calculation agent. Find two state pooling associations with wildfire or hail exposure, get indications of interest from two ILS funds, and produce a reusable term-sheet template. Charge a structuring retainer to fund first-deal work.

title: Reproduction-Gated Vulnerability Inbox for Maintainers
one_liner: A hosted security-report intake that only forwards a report if its proof-of-concept actually reproduces against the maintainer's tagged release in a sandbox, so AI-generated slop dies before a human reads it.
customer: Maintainers and foundations of widely depended-on open-source projects (paid by corporate sponsors and dependents), plus small vendors that must run a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy under the CRA. They pay $99-499/month per project, or $2k/month sponsor-funded shields for critical projects.
problem: curl ended its bug bounty at the end of January 2026 to 'remove the incentive for people to submit crap and non-well researched reports... AI generated or not'; in the week before, 7 submissions contained no real vulnerabilities but still burned security-team time. Maintainers are also drowning in PRs, with Ladybird banning non-maintainer PRs and Rust's Clippy gamifying review, while companies float donating AI credits to maintainers instead.
solution: An intake form and GitHub App that requires a machine-checkable reproducer (Dockerfile/script/HTTP request plus the expected oracle, such as an ASAN crash, unexpected file read or assertion). The service builds the project at the reported tag in a microVM, runs the reproducer and only escalates reports that trip the oracle. Failures get instant automated feedback. Passing reports arrive at the maintainer as a verified repro bundle, deduplicated against past reports, with a suggested severity and a drafted advisory and CVE request. Logic bugs without automatic oracles go through a refundable deposit lane. Start with memory-safety classes (C/C++/Rust/Go) where oracles are objective.
why_now: January 2026 made the AI-slop-versus-security-report problem concrete and public. CRA reporting duties began in September 2026, increasing report volume and the need for a documented intake. Cheap microVM sandboxes (Firecracker-class) make per-report verification cost cents.
revenue_model: Sponsor-paid subscriptions: $99-499/month per project, funded by the top dependents (companies that already say they want to help maintainers, per the AI-credits thread). $1-2k/month for critical projects. Per-verified-report fee for small vendors with public VDPs.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone argues about banning submissions or paying for them; nobody has moved the burden of proof onto machines, and the same LLMs that write slop cannot fake a crashing sanitizer trace on the maintainer's own build. The buyer is not the burned-out maintainer with no budget but the dependents who need that maintainer to keep going. Evidence: curl closing its bounty https://www.theregister.com/2026/01/21/curl_ends_bug_bounty/; maintainers asking how to handle PR slop and pointing to tools https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47492078; Ladybird and Clippy approaches plus a call for third-party solutions https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48949019; companies wanting to donate but debating the wrong instrument (credits vs money) https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48346013.
first_30_days: Build the GitHub App and intake page for C, Rust and Go projects using sanitizer/crash oracles. Recruit 3 mid-size maintainers by replying in the PR-slop and AI-contribution Ask HN threads; run their real inbox through it in shadow mode for two weeks and report the percentage of reports filtered. Take that data to each project's top corporate dependents and ask for a $250/month sponsorship that funds the shield.

title: Pay-Per-Decibel Neighbor Trust for Data Centers
one_liner: An independent trust that owns a sensor mesh around a data center and automatically pays nearby households every time the hum exceeds agreed limits, turning 'trust us' into a self-executing contract.
customer: Data center developers and hyperscaler community-affairs teams, their land-use counsel, and counties negotiating community benefit agreements. Pre-application projects facing a rezoning fight are the entry point.
problem: Local opposition blocked or delayed roughly $130B of US data center projects in 2026, and opposition groups more than doubled to 833 by March. Developers' flat checks get called bribes: a $10,000-per-household offer to 4,500 households was rejected by residents in September. Noise promises are unenforceable, and dBA ordinances miss the low-frequency hum residents complain about. Counties lack staff to monitor compliance.
solution: A neighbor trust, funded by a developer bond, with three parts. (1) Trust-owned acoustic, low-frequency and vibration sensors, publicly viewable in real time. (2) A pre-agreed parametric schedule: any household within the radius gets an automatic payment for each night the level exceeds the threshold, so the payout works like a warranty on quiet. (3) Escalation funding for window and HVAC retrofits if exceedances persist. The trust also reports compliance to the county, giving regulators enforcement without new staff.
why_now: Opposition is peaking (about 120 projects stalled in H1 2026, more than 300 state bills, moratoria such as New York's), and developers are now experimenting with direct household payments and getting burned on credibility. Developers now need a neutral administrator, and no obvious specialist exists.
revenue_model: Developer pays $150k to $500k setup per campus, plus 8% to 12% of the annual fund as administration, plus sensor-as-a-service fees. Add county compliance-monitoring contracts. A single multi-billion-dollar campus can absorb this as a rounding error against months of delay.
non_obvious_insight: Neighbors rarely reject data centers over money. They reject unmeasured, unpriced harm. Making the harm measured and self-paying changes the negotiation and gives the developer a real financial reason to buy quieter chillers and dampers. The low-frequency, night-time signature is what the trust measures, and ordinances miss it.
first_30_days: List the next five county hearings on data center rezoning from local news and Data Center Watch. Hire a freelance acoustic engineer and build a $2k-per-node sensor kit from off-the-shelf parts. Offer a free 60-day neutral baseline noise map to one pending project, in front of both the developer and the opposition group. Convert that goodwill into a paid pre-application baseline of $50k to $100k and an MOU for the trust structure.

title: Verbal-Promise Ledger for Mine Community Relations
one_liner: A voice-first, offline-capable phone tool that turns every promise a mine makes at community assemblies (Spanish, Quechua, Aymara) into a tracked commitment register the community can verify by WhatsApp.
customer: Heads of social performance and community relations at mid-tier copper and lithium operators and developers in Peru, Chile, Argentina and Bolivia. The second buyer is the E&S team at the lender or DFI (IFC, EXIM, DFC, export credit agencies). Budget is roughly $2-6k per month per project, charged to a risk or permitting line, not to IT.
problem: Insiders know that projects get blockaded over small, forgotten verbal promises, not over the headline issue. Examples are a promised well repair, a local-hire quota, or a dust-suppression schedule. The promise is made at a 2pm assembly and recorded on a paper acta, in a notebook, or in a WhatsApp voice note. Community-relations staff rotate every 12-24 months, contractors make their own promises, and nobody indexes the actas. Two years later the community says 'you promised' and shuts the road. The Las Bambas corridor closures, Jujuy lithium protests and Tia Maria all fit this pattern of trust debt. The mine cannot prove what it did or did not commit to, and neither can the community.
solution: Field officers record assemblies on a phone and snap a photo of the signed acta. Speech-to-text, tuned for Andean Spanish and human-checked for Quechua and Aymara, extracts discrete commitments: who promised what, to whom, and by when. Each one is assigned an internal owner and a due date. Community leaders get a receipt as a WhatsApp voice note or pictogram and can confirm, dispute, or mark it done. Ops managers and the CFO see 'commitment debt' aging, like a technical-debt dashboard. One-click exports meet IFC Performance Standard 1 and Equator Principles grievance and commitment register requirements. Community-side verification is the moat. It makes this a trust tool, not a surveillance tool.
why_now: Speech models are good enough for accented, code-switched Spanish, and usable for Quechua with a human in the loop. WhatsApp is universal in rural Andean communities. Lenders are demanding auditable social-license evidence for critical-mineral financings, including EU CRMA strategic projects and US DOE/DFC/EXIM deals. Argentina's RIGI regime is pulling lithium and copper projects into provinces with little consultation history. Peru and Chile have changed governments (2026), which reopens community negotiations. Staff turnover after the 2024-25 cost-cutting rounds has made institutional memory worse.
revenue_model: SaaS at $2-6k per month per project, plus a per-community onboarding fee ($1-3k). A one-off 'commitment debt audit' of historical actas is priced at $5-15k. Later, a lender-grade verified engagement score and a lender or insurer data licence.
non_obvious_insight: Conflict risk is mostly commitment debt, meaning unanswered small promises lost through staff rotation, not big ideological opposition. Buyers think they need sentiment analysis. What they need is a receipt system. Giving the community the receipt is what makes the mine's data credible to lenders and inspectors.
first_30_days: Through ex-colleagues, recruit two junior or mid-tier developers currently in a consultation round. Sell a $5-10k 'commitment debt audit': scan their last 12 months of actas and meeting minutes, and use an LLM plus a local linguist to extract every commitment and flag the overdue ones. This works with no integration, just PDFs and photos. The overdue list is usually shocking, and it converts to a SaaS pilot for the next assembly round. Use a WhatsApp Business API bot and an offline recorder app for v1. Do not build a custom platform yet.

title: Glasses-Free Zone: Smart-Glasses Detection Kits
one_liner: A detection-plus-policy kit for rooms where camera glasses cannot be allowed (exam centers, courtrooms, medical rooms, locker rooms, poker rooms), with logged, defensible procedures.
customer: Independent test centers, licensing and language-test operators, court administrators, casinos and poker rooms, med-spas, therapy and medical offices, gyms and locker-room operators.
problem: Camera and AI glasses look like ordinary eyewear and are now cheap and everywhere. Venues have bans on paper but no way to enforce or prove violations. In May 2026 two TOEIC test-takers were caught with AI glasses and banned for four years. The College Board banned smart glasses (even prescription ones) at the SAT starting March 2026, and New York State courts banned them across all courthouses in 2026.
solution: A door-frame or desk unit combining Bluetooth and Wi-Fi signature scanning for known glasses families, plus an optional optical check for camera lenses. It ships with a written policy pack, non-accusatory staff scripts, signage, a tamper-evident event log usable in score-invalidation or eviction disputes, and a short staff certification. The software updates as new glasses launch.
why_now: Camera-and-AI glasses went mainstream in 2025 to 2026, and other brands are launching. Institutions responded with bans in months, but incumbents (exam vendors, courts, gyms) have no tooling or procedures. The 18-month gap is between glasses in millions of faces and venue-grade controls. Consumer detector apps exist, but no one owns the evidence-grade, staff-friendly layer.
revenue_model: $299 to $999 policy and training kit, $1,500 to $5,000 per site for hardware install, then $49 to $149 per month for signature updates, incident logging and re-certification.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer's problem isn't detection accuracy, it's defensibility. A test center that cancels a score or a court that ejects a spectator needs a repeatable, logged, non-accusatory process to survive an appeal or a complaint. Sell the paper trail and the staff script, and treat the sensor as an accessory. False accusations, not misses, are what scare institutions.
first_30_days: Build a prototype scanner on an ESP32 or Raspberry Pi with known Bluetooth signatures from Ray-Ban Meta and other glasses, and test on real devices. Write the policy kit with an ex-proctor or court-security advisor. Offer paid pilots to 10 independent test-prep and test centers, one poker room and two med-spas. Charge for the kit from the start.

title: Article 50 Compliance-in-a-Box for GenAI Apps
one_liner: An SDK and audit pack that adds machine-readable AI-output marking and disclosure to small generative apps before 2 Dec 2026.
customer: Indie and mid-size generative image, audio and video app makers and API resellers selling into the EU. There are thousands of them.
problem: EU AI Act Article 50(2) requires generative systems to mark outputs in a machine-readable format, and systems already on the market must comply by 2 Dec 2026, about nine weeks away. Small vendors cannot afford lawyers and do not know the standards. Fines are material.
solution: A drop-in library or proxy that embeds C2PA manifests, invisible watermarks and metadata for text, audio, image and video outputs, plus a verification endpoint. It generates an audit-ready evidence file, disclosure text for deployers, and tracks code-of-practice updates.
why_now: The deadline is imminent and enforcement risk is real. Most small AI apps have done nothing, and big vendors' tooling covers only their own models.
revenue_model: $199-1,500 per month for app makers, $30K+ enterprise, and paid verification API usage.
non_obvious_insight: The compliance wave hits the long tail that cannot afford counsel. Watermark tech is commoditized, but audit evidence, ongoing updates and a verification endpoint are what buyers pay for.
first_30_days: Ship an SDK for image and audio APIs commonly wrapped by indie apps. Launch a landing page with a countdown, sell 30 subscriptions at $299 per month through indie and EU AI-Act communities, and publish a free checklist.

title: Test-once PFAS proof registry for packaging importers
one_liner: A SKU-level registry and group-buy of accredited PFAS lab reports, so importers of the same factory's food packaging share one test and can produce an authority-ready dossier fast.
customer: EU importers, wholesalers and white-label brands of grease-resistant paper and fibre food packaging (takeaway boxes, bakery bags, burger wraps, pizza boxes, cups), plus online B2B packaging shops. Owners, purchasing or QA managers pay.
problem: Since 12 Aug 2026 the packaging regulation bans PFAS in food-contact packaging above limits (25 ppb per non-polymeric substance, 250 ppb sum, 50 ppm total PFAS), with no grandfathering for stock made earlier. Compliance guides say supplier self-declarations are not proof and that importers and producers carry the liability, with accredited-lab reports needed per packaging type. Authorities can request the technical documentation on short notice. There is no harmonised EU test method and lab capacity is finite. Each importer paying separately for the same factory's product is wasteful.
solution: A registry keyed to product specification, coating, factory and production lot. Factories, labs and importers upload accredited lab reports (cheap total organic fluorine screening first, then targeted LC-MS/MS). Other importers of the same factory and spec can match and attach the report to their own technical file. A lot-matching check and re-test reminders keep the proof valid, and an 'authority request pack' export assembles the file in one click. Group-buy: when several importers sell the same SKU, the platform pools the cost of one accredited test and negotiates volume prices with 2-3 labs. Each importer remains legally responsible, so the tool shows exactly what evidence it does and does not cover.
why_now: The ban applied on 12 Aug 2026, six weeks ago, and stock made before then cannot be sold. Labs expect demand to climb through enforcement and there is no harmonised method yet, so evidence quality varies.
revenue_model: EUR 150-400 per verified report access, EUR 25 per month per SKU for monitoring and re-test alerts, plus a 10-15% margin on group-purchased lab tests. Optional paid dossier assembly at EUR 300-600.
non_obvious_insight: Every importer treats PFAS proof as its own cost, but the object being proven is the packaging type. The same few hundred factory SKUs flow through thousands of importers, which creates network effects for a 'test once, verify per lot' registry that no consultancy or lab has an incentive to build. Evidence: guides state that 'self-declarations from suppliers do not constitute proof' and that certificates of analysis are needed per packaging type (https://www.certivo.com/blog-details/ppwr-pfas-ban-in-food-contact-packaging-what-manufacturers-must-have-ready-by-august-2026); the ban has no grandfather clause and responsibility falls on manufacturers and importers (https://www.kivo.nl/en/knowledge-base/pfas-ban-in-food-packaging-what-does-it-mean-for-your-products/); testing runs from a few hundred euros for screening to several thousand for targeted analysis, labs have limited capacity, and no harmonised EU method exists (https://pakfactory.com/blog/how-to-test-packaging-for-pfas; https://foodpackagingforum.org/news/ppwr-pfas-limits-apply-from-august-12).
first_30_days: Sign volume pricing with 2 accredited labs for TOF screening and targeted panels. Recruit 10 importers from packaging trade associations, LinkedIn groups and B2B packaging marketplaces. Ask them to list their top 20 SKUs and factories, then find overlaps between them. Run the first pooled test for the most-shared SKU at a per-importer cost far below a solo test. Publish a free 'PFAS status per SKU' lookup to attract more importers. Legal-review the shared-report disclaimer language with a food-contact lawyer.

title: Bereavement Aftercare for Independent Funeral Homes
one_liner: A white-label 13-month aftercare program that funeral homes buy to keep the newly widowed connected after the casseroles stop.
customer: Independent funeral homes (roughly 18,000 in the US, mostly independent), paying $200-350 per family served or a flat monthly fee.
problem: Grief tech money chases griefbots and digital memorials. The real gap is months 2-13, when widowhood drives isolation, depression and elevated mortality. Funeral directors hold the only list of newly bereaved households and a position of trust, but 'aftercare' is usually a brochure and a card. Cremation rates above 60% shrink revenue per call, and independents need loyalty and pre-need referrals to survive against consolidators.
solution: A packaged program: scheduled outreach calls at day 3, 14, 30 and 90, plus first-holiday and anniversary contacts. Small 'second-Thursday' peer groups hosted in the funeral home's own room. A paperwork concierge for Social Security, pensions and accounts, which is the logistics half of grief. A prolonged-grief screener at 6 months with referral to partner clinicians. Software runs scripts, scheduling, facilitator rosters and flags.
why_now: WHO's 2025 framing of loneliness as a measured global health metric gives directors a vocabulary and a reason to act. Rising cremation share squeezes revenue per family. Boomer-parent deaths are rising. Independents are hunting a differentiator against Service Corporation International-style chains.
revenue_model: $200-350 per family served billed to the funeral home, plus referral fees from partner therapists and an uplift in pre-need sales the home can attribute to the program.
non_obvious_insight: Griefbot founders sell to the bereaved at their worst moment. The natural customer for grief is the funeral director, who owns the list, is paid nothing after day 3, and buys aftercare as a marketing and retention expense at his best moment.
first_30_days: Sell 5 funeral homes at $300 per family through state funeral-director association meetings. Hire two part-time facilitators (hospice social workers). Run the first second-Thursday group. Track 6-month contact retention and pre-need referrals as the proof for the next 50 homes.

title: Flash-Heated Graphite Restoration From Anode Scrap
one_liner: Use flash Joule heating to restore spent and scrap anode graphite to usable grade in seconds, giving US anode makers a domestic, non-Chinese feedstock.
customer: US anode makers and cell manufacturers needing non-Chinese graphite (buyers), and cell-plant scrap managers (feedstock sellers).
problem: Graphite is a large share of black-mass weight, and hydromet recyclers typically treat it as waste. China dominates anode graphite, has tightened graphite export licensing, and the US has almost no domestic supply.
solution: A pulsed reactor (flash Joule heating, from academic work at Rice) purifies and re-graphitizes anode scrap at about 3000 K in seconds, using far less energy than conventional graphitization furnaces. The first product is a 100 kg/day pilot line producing qualification samples, with early sales into non-battery markets while battery-grade qualification proceeds.
why_now: Chinese graphite controls, US trade remedies, and rising domestic cell-plant scrap volumes all arrived in the last two years, and flash processing moved from lab papers to pilots.
revenue_model: Tolling or per-kg sale priced against imported anode-grade graphite, plus grants and offtake advance payments.
non_obvious_insight: Graphite is the one battery material that recycling plants throw away while the US has essentially no domestic supply.
first_30_days: License or build a bench flash reactor. Collect 500 kg of anode scrap from a cell-plant scrapper. Produce samples and send to 3 anode makers or national labs for coin-cell testing. File for DOE or DoD SBIR funding.
